reviews.review: Wokehammer. Vote with Your wallet. Purge DEI cancer

So I watched some gameplay of the sequel and might say its good it did not disappoint and I retracted for what I said.

But two things I still dont like
1. the price of the first game
2. I do not trust GW

The Warhammer franchise is dead, they are rewriting the lore to make it more LGBT friendly, because of course the brutal fascist patriarchal dictatorship of the distant future would support equality and trans rights! They even hired an openly racist writer for Space Marine 2 because her kind of racism is approved by the DEI ESG corporate fascists of today.
If you want to fight for the future of humanity against corporate fascism stop paying for all Warhammer products.

Now, I'm sure this will upset someone who loves Warhammer 40k, but I'm sorr-- no, I'm not sorry; this game could've been something great, but it has some real bad design choices. Don't get me wrong, some things in Space Marine are good, such as the sound, voices, and general aesthetics, but that's it; it's pretty much style over substance.

The way the game looks is very nice. The Space Marines, Orks and Chaos are all modelled really well; big, bulky and intimidating (shame there were no Terminators, though). It has the locations down, but really only has ONE and that is a massive, dusty, gothic-looking city with some sewers and mechanised interiors. Even when you enter a Warp touched structure at the end of the game it only has floating debris/platforms and a hint of purple in the air. It was fine to start with but it all drags by the end of the six to seven hour campaign. Yes, only six to seven hours; I hope you enjoy the combat as the multiplayer will be the only thing making your £39.99 purchase go further.

The gameplay? THIS is where most of my complaints stem. It starts off well enough where you're mowing down Gretchins and low-tier Orks -- getting those glory-kills in and what-not -- but when the bigger enemies start coming in, that is when the cracks start to show. Your melee attacks -- even when using a weapon that supposedly is good for armoured enemies -- don't stagger; making you back-pedal, firing your Bolter into their faces and maybe dodging if they take a swing at you. Your best bet for close range is the Meltagun, or the Lascannon for long range if you have time before the bigger enemies catch up to you.

Your health bar and shields are a joke; sometimes your shield just empties after about four hits and your health can drop equally as fast, but you can replenish some health by doing glory-kills on stunned enemies. That's neat, you might think, but... no, not with the way this game has it. 
First and foremost, you can still take damage while doing glory-kills, which is really infuriating when you're just about to get your health back and some little turd slaps you on the arse to finish you off.
Secondly, you need to grab a stunned enemy to do the glory-kills; so, yet again, some little turd could come along and stand in your path when you press the command to perform the kill, making you just gently caress the one blocking you.

Wow, this is going on for a while, but I'm nearly done. Finally -- for the glory-kill mechanic, anyway -- it becomes a lot harder, bordering on impossible, to do this toward the end of the game when it decides it wants to be more like Gears of War; oh, but then grenades when you take cover, forcing you out, and if you dare to charge for some melee you'll soon see your shield and health disappear.

Some of the weapons are good, and the rest were just outclassed; you can only carry five weapons, as well, one of those being your melee weapon. The Bolter never gets replaced and is your main gun for the whole game; good thing it's one of the best weapons. The Storm Bolter... sucks; at least for me, anyway. It fires more rapidly than the Bolter but has much more spread, making it a close range gun, but is completely outclassed by the Meltagun. The Meltagun is just a good weapon for the high-tier enemies, but has limited ammo. The Lascannon is the best sniper gun as long as your aim is true, as it also has limited ammo. The sniper Bolter is the only other scoped gun but is a decent replacement if you run out of Lascannon ammo. The Vengeance Launcher was... fine, until I got the Meltagun, then I never used it again. The plasma gun would have been much better if it didn't take the slot of your scoped gun, so... yeah.

*Sigh* I liked this game to start with, but it becomes a slog and infuriating. If you enjoy this game, then more power to you; I picked this game up dirt cheap before the anniversary edition came out, so I was lucky. Apologies for this rant of a review, but maybe it's because I like Warhammer 40k (mostly the models) that I wanted this to be a great game.
